text:
harry: noticing elevated host CPU on proxy nodes after kernel-picker v2. p99 tokenization tails increased and grpc small-write syscalls spiked. attaching quick flame excerpt. anyone seen similar? :eyes:

tess: which pool? sample flame pls and write syscall counters. my gut: kernel-path mismatch + write coalescing not firing.

harry: eu-west1 proxy pool. flame top: 
```
  48% host::tokenize_line
  30% net::grpc::emit_writev
  12% parse::chunk_split
  10% kernel::dispatch_slow
```
writev rate ~9 calls per 1KB output, lots of 64-256b frames.

omar: around the same time the kvcache per-shard eviction rate jumped. Could be batching window shrinkage causing prefixes to flush before cache warms. Do we have per-shard histograms?

harry: quick snapshot: kvcache hit 0.83 -> 0.68 during spike, evictions/sec 320 -> 1100, avg_lookup_ns 430 -> 920.

tess: that smells like batching hysteresis. kernel-picker changed preference for eager-kernel which may reduce user-thread syscall count for small requests but pushes serialization earlier for long sequences. we should test a config matrix.

omar: agree. propose matrix: 
- 1 (base): kernel_prefer=eager_off, batch.window_ms=2
- 2: kernel_prefer=eager_on, batch.window_ms=2
- 3: kernel_prefer=eager_on, batch.window_ms=12
- 4: kernel_prefer=eager_on, batch.window_ms=12 + microbatch(count=3,max_delay=6ms)
Run synthetic mixed workload: 96% short (8-24 tokens) + 4% long (600-900 tokens). Measure: p50/p95/p99 host CPU, tokenize wall time, writev syscalls/request, kvcache histograms, and end-to-end latency SLOs.

harry: started 3 on a small canary. perf-bot: /perf run --matrix=3 --traces=kvcache,writev,flame.

perf-bot: canary-3-3245679999 deployed. perf link: https://perf.internal/runs/32456799 (results pending).

omar: quick interim from canary-3: small req CPU -6%, long req p99 +3.1%, kvcache hit 0.79, evictions/sec 560, writev counts reduced for short flows but increased for long flows.

tess: that confirms tradeoff. microbatcher likely to help mixed loads by coalescing small writes without hurting long-seq batching too much. but microbatcher can add tail ms for tiny bursts; need to bound max_delay.

harry: also noticed transport-level coalescing flags (`transport.write_coalesce=true`) were set but TCP_NODELAY and explicit flush points from the runtime can override. we should audit flush callsites in tokenizer/streamer.

omar: second hypothesis: kernel-picker may select a kernel variant that allocates intermediate buffers on host path earlier, increasing tokenize serialize time. we should add microbench to measure serialize_ns per-token for each kernel variant.

tess: good call. add a kernel-variant microbench that cycles kernel variants and measures: serialize_ns, syscall_count_per_kb, kv_lookups_per_request. also capture flame for host thread.

harry: infra started matrix 1/2/3/4 across 4 canary groups. ops-bot posted CSVs to perf.

ops-bot: runs uploaded: https://perf.internal/csvs/32456799-matrix.zip. includes per-shard kvcache histos and syscall counters.

omar: looked at CSVs. summary: matrix-4 (microbatch + window=12 + eager_on) gives best mixed workload: overall host p99 -5% vs baseline, kvcache evictions down ~45%, writev syscalls/request down ~60% on short flows, long flow p99 unchanged within noise. p50 small-request latency increased by ~0.9ms due to microbatch delay.

tess: tradeoffs seem acceptable but need to ensure SLOs. propose temporary rollout config: `kernel_prefer=eager_on`, `batch.window_ms=12`, `microbatch(count=3,max_delay_ms=6)`, keep `transport.write_coalesce=true`. Also add kernel-variant serialize microbench as regression test.

harry: I'll file PERF-1242 with hypothesis, attach flames, CSVs, and recommended interim config. will include steps to revert kernel-picker if regressions show.

omar: I'll add a per-commit perf check to kernel-picker PR that runs the microbench and validates serialize_ns doesn't regress >10% for common kernels.

tess: action items: 
- harry: create perf ticket + rollback playbook (target today).
- omar: add microbench + CI gating for kernel-picker.
- tess: audit flush callsites in tokenizer/streamer and open a follow-up to make coalescing more deterministic (maybe defer flushes to IO thread).

harry: kicking off the ticket now and tagging people. will update when rollout starts. :thumbsup:
